title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: reserve a free room on the spot from the console
summary: Hold: the role-assignment requirement omits Microsoft's documented option to use a custom role with role-management permissions. The statement that console reservation display details are undocumented is also too broad: Microsoft documents the room calendar's displayed fields and privacy behavior. The roadmap facts, Pro licensing and reservation toggle are supported.

claims.where: Governance controls: creating and editing roles
claims.claim: Creating or editing portal roles requires Global Administrator, Teams Administrator or Teams Rooms Pro Manager permissions.
claims.quote: Teams Administrator or Teams Devices Administrator assigned to an Administrative Unit (AU), can't access the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal, as AUs aren't currently supported.
claims.fix: Qualify Teams Administrator as tenant-wide in the role requirement: 'Creating or editing portal roles requires Global Administrator, tenant-wide Teams Administrator, or Teams Rooms Pro Manager.' Apply together with the assignment correction below. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-pro-rbac.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: assigning roles
claims.claim: Assigning portal roles requires Global Administrator, Teams Administrator or Teams Rooms Pro Manager.
claims.quote: To assign roles, you must be a Global Administrator/ Teams Administrator or Teams Rooms Pro Manager role or have a custom role with role management permissions.
claims.fix: Replace the assignment requirement in controls[1].note and the matching table note with 'Assigning roles requires Global Administrator, tenant-wide Teams Administrator, Teams Rooms Pro Manager, or a custom role with role management permissions.' In Governance controls, replace the combined requirement sentence with 'Creating or editing portal roles requires Global Administrator, tenant-wide Teams Administrator, or Teams Rooms Pro Manager. Assigning roles also permits a custom role with role management permissions.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-pro-rbac; its note says an Administrative Unit-scoped Teams Administrator cannot access the portal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new data reach beyond booking the meeting room.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Windows ad hoc room reservation Reserve organizer identity duration calendar processing Exchange privacy data. Read home screen, release notes and resource-account search excerpts; the reservation description names room booking, not additional data access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document which account appears as organizer for a Windows console reservation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms" "reservation" "organizer" "duration" console Windows. Read home screen, release notes and panel-reservation search excerpts; the panel-specific organizer statement does not establish Windows console behavior.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: What the console shows of a room-calendar reservation is not documented.
claims.quote: By default, room users can join meetings in one touch and view meeting details including the meeting name, organizer, time, and platform. ... meeting names can be hidden ... and replaced with the organizer name if desired
claims.fix: Narrow the sentence to 'Who the booking shows as organiser is not documented; check on a test room before relying on meeting-name privacy settings.' Remove 'and what the console shows of it': https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/mtr-home-refresh documents the general room-calendar display fields and meeting-name privacy behavior, even though it does not identify the organizer account or generated subject for this reservation.
